statements.text: The patient reports a sore throat for about 3 days with marked pain on swallowing, even water.
The patient measured a temperature of 38.5 last night and reports chills.
The patient denies cough, runny nose, or nasal congestion and reports a feeling of neck swelling.
The patient's roommate was diagnosed with strep throat last week.
The patient has been taking ibuprofen 400 mg about twice a day with slight relief.
The patient is allergic to penicillin, with hives from amoxicillin in childhood.
The patient has no other medical problems and takes no regular medications.
Temperature 38.3, heart rate 96, blood pressure 118/76.
Tonsils are swollen with bilateral white exudate.
Anterior cervical lymph nodes are enlarged and tender.
Ears appear normal and lungs are clear.
Rapid strep test is positive.
Strep pharyngitis, supported by fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes, absence of cough, and positive rapid strep test.
